content.one_sentence_role: Applies the open connected theorem to two positive-radius balls.
content.natural_language_statement: Let $E,F$ be real normed spaces, $c\in E$, $d\in F$, and $r,R>0$. For a bijective isometry $f:B(c,r)\to B(d,R)$ there exists a unique surjective real affine isometry $A:E\to F$ satisfying $A(x)=f(x)$ for all $x\in B(c,r)$.
content.assumptions: Both radii are positive. They are not assumed equal. No nonzero-dimension or completeness hypothesis is imposed on the spaces.
content.conclusion: The specified isometry of open balls has exactly one ambient affine-isometry extension.
content.proof_summary: Check openness and nonempty connectedness of the source ball, then substitute the two balls into the open connected theorem.
proof_steps: The two balls are open. Since $r>0$, $c\in B(c,r)$, and this ball is convex: for $x,y$ in it and $0\le a\le1$, $\|(1-a)x+ay-c\|\le(1-a)\|x-c\|+a\|y-c\|<r$. Thus it is nonempty and connected. Positivity of $R$ also makes the target ball nonempty and connected, although target connectedness is not an independent input to the next theorem.

Apply [Open connected extension theorem](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Affine/IsometryExtension/OpenConnected.lean#L120-L147) with $s=B(c,r)$, $t=B(d,R)$ and the given $f$. The openness and source connectedness just verified supply its hypotheses. Its single existence-and-uniqueness conclusion gives $A(x)=f(x)$ for every source-ball point, exactly as required.
